Subject: Proposal: staged capacity synchronization & co-term approach for Acuity Health renewal

Hi Margaret / Tim —

Thanks again for the productive renewal discussion last week. Attached is a first-pass proposal that attempts to balance Acuity's need for predictable unit economics with your phased rollout over the next 18 months. High level:

- Term: 24 months (co-term across hospitals to a single renewal date)
- Staged committed ramp: 0–3 months (onboarding), then 3-month step ups at 3, 6, 9, 12 months to reach target committed throughput (see SOW_Annex_A_Staged_Ramp.xlsx)
- Pricing: blended committed rate with two-tier discounts — 10% off list in year 1 for the staged commit, 5% off in year 2; true-ups quarterly
- Auto-renew: optional; procurement asked for opt-out window — we propose a 60-day notice before renewal to allow non-renew without penalty
- Co-terming: we can align existing division contracts to a single co-term start of 2026-10-01 to simplify billing and support

I flagged a couple of items where we occasionally grant short-term capacity bursts during onboarding (subject to transient overage rates) and noted an SLA credit schedule in the appendix.

Please review the attached PDF + SOW annex and let me know what questions procurement needs answered (evidence, audit logs, billing specifics). If this looks directionally correct I can push a DocuSign package and schedule a pre-sign kickoff.

Thanks —
Priyom
Enterprise Renewals | Redwood Inference
priom.das@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0133

Attachments: Redwood_Renewal_Proposal_Q3-2026.pdf (proposal summary), SOW_Annex_A_Staged_Ramp.xlsx (detailed ramp schedule)

Hi Priyom —

Thanks for the proposal and the clear ramp schedule. A couple quick clarifying questions from our side:

1) The 10% first-year discount — does that require the full 24-month commit up front, or is it tied to hitting the ramp milestones?
2) Our procurement team needs explicit language allowing a 60-day non-renew opt-out without automatic penalties. Can you confirm that will be in the contract?
3) If we need capacity earlier than the schedule (unexpected uptake), what is the process for escalating capacity and how are overage charges calculated?

Procurement looped in. Tim — I can make time this Thursday afternoon for a short call if helpful.

Best,
Margaret
Director, AI Platform | Acuity Health
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Proposal: staged capacity synchronization & co-term approach for Acuity Health renewal

Priyom — looping in operations notes for the proposed schedule. Quoting Margaret's questions below for context:

> 1) The 10% first-year discount — does that require the full 24-month commit up front, or is it tied to hitting the ramp milestones?
> 2) Our procurement team needs explicit language allowing a 60-day non-renew opt-out without automatic penalties. Can you confirm that will be in the contract?
> 3) If we need capacity earlier than the schedule (unexpected uptake), what is the process for escalating capacity and how are overage charges calculated?

Answers from ops perspective:
- Discount: we typically require an executed 24-month MSA + SOW for the introductory discount; the discount is not milestone-contingent, but we do include quarterly true-ups so customers are only billed for committed + true-up. We can offer a conditional clawback if the ramp never reaches 70% of committed after 12 months, but that's negotiable.
- Opt-out: 60-day opt-out before renewal is acceptable; procurement language should be explicit about notice window and final true-up obligations.
- Escalation: we can do capacity bursts via a pre-approved burst pool (billed at burst-overage rate). If customer wants permanent earlier capacity, we amend the SOW to accelerate the next step and prorate commitments for the remaining term. Overage calc: prorated per-token/embedding rate + 25% premium for burst hours.

Operational ask: confirm whether co-terming will consolidate three existing purchase orders into a single SOW with start date 2026-10-01. That impacts billing alignment and the way we run true-ups.

-Monica
Principal, Customer Success Operations
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Margaret Hsu <margaret.hsu@acuityhealth.com>, Tim Collins <tim.collins@acuityhealth.com>

Date: Fri, 6 Aug 2026 14:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: staged capacity synchronization & co-term approach for Acuity Health renewal

Margaret / Tim —

Thanks — and great questions. Quick summary and next steps:

- The 10% first-year discount is tied to the executed 24-month MSA + SOW (we require signature to lock the rate), not on achieving each milestone; billing is based on committed units + quarterly true-ups. We will add a clause for a 12-month performance review and can include a limited clawback if <70% of committed throughput is reached after 12 months (this is optional language — happy to remove if not needed).
- We will add explicit 60-day non-renew opt-out language in the contractual DocuSign bundle so procurement is comfortable. No early termination penalty beyond the final true-up for usage through the opt-out date.
- Escalation path: immediate burst via pre-approved burst pool (billed at burst rate). For permanent increases we execute an SOW amendment; we will prorate future commitments. Overage rate example included in appendix.

Attached: updated proposal PDF and SOW annex (same filenames as referenced). I pushed an editable DocuSign packet: https://na1.docusign.net/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?PowerFormId=abcdef-12345 — it contains MSA + SOW with the 60-day opt-out language in the renewal section and a table for the staged ramp pricing.

High-level ramp excerpt (committed QPS equivalents):
- Month 0–3: onboarding (10% of target baseline)
- Month 4–6: 35% of target baseline
- Month 7–9: 65% of target baseline
- Month 10–12: 100% of target baseline (full committed coverage)

If you confirm co-term start 2026-10-01 we will consolidate the three POs into a single SOW with that effective date and align billing for quarterly true-ups on the calendar quarter boundaries.

Request: can procurement review the packet this week so legal + finance can sign before 2026-08-20? If so I will schedule a 30-minute pre-sign kickoff for the week of Aug 16.

Thanks —
Priyom
